title: Kronjakt (Crown Hunt) contract
description: Language-neutral Kronjakt shapes shared by iOS, Android, backend, and admin. crownHuntPoint mirrors `crownHuntPoints/{pointId}` and crownHuntClaim mirrors `crownHuntClaims/{claimId}` (docs/firebase-data-model.md). The backend is the sole authority for eligibility, claims, and Kronpoäng awards — clients never calculate or award points, claims are never automatic, and awards commit atomically with the claim record. Risk scores/reasons are backend-only and never appear in these client-facing shapes. Firestore stores timestamps as native Timestamp values; this contract describes their ISO 8601 JSON serialization.

crownHuntPointStatus.description: Only active points are visible to members. Activation is a safety-gated admin step.

crownHuntClaimResult.description: Eligibility failures are result codes with Swedish user messages, not errors (legacy parity).

crownHuntPoint.description: Firestore `crownHuntPoints/{pointId}`. Active members read active points; all writes via admin crownHunt.* callables.

title.description: Optional label; empty string when the point has no title.

maxCollectors.description: How many distinct users may collect this crown. null = unlimited (default). A positive integer caps the headcount: the first N distinct collectors succeed, then the point is deactivated (status 'ended'). Clients may show remaining slots as maxCollectors - collectorCount.

collectorCount.description: Distinct users who have collected this crown so far. 0 for unlimited or freshly-created points; maintained by the backend only.

crownHuntClaim.description: Firestore `crownHuntClaims/{claimId}` — every claim ATTEMPT. Document ID = SHA-256(userId ':' idempotencyKey). Owner-only member read; written only by crownHunt.submitClaim. Risk data lives in the backend-only crownHuntClaimRisk collection, never here.

submitClaimRequest.description: Input for crownHunt.submitClaim (member-only). The position must be fresh (<=60 s) and the reported speed at or below walking pace (~1.4 m/s) — claiming requires being safely stopped. Distance is always computed server-side.

accuracyMeters.description: Reported horizontal GPS accuracy. Client-supplied, so it is bounded: larger (or non-finite) values are rejected as invalid-argument, and the value that reaches the geofence buffer is clamped server-side — the buffered fence can never exceed twice the point's configured radius.

idempotencyKey.description: Fresh per button press; retries of the same press reuse it and replay the stored result.

platformIntegrityPassed.description: Play Integrity / App Attest placeholder — null until native integration.

createPointRequest.description: Input for crownHunt.createPoint (admin). Points are created as drafts. A Crown is a map collectable (Pokémon GO–style), not a titled document — no title/description is accepted; rewardPoints comes from a rarity tier chosen in the admin UI. The stored crownHuntPoint still carries title ('') and description (null) for reader back-compat.

maxCollectors.description: How many distinct users may collect this crown. null (or omitted) = unlimited (default, best for events). A positive integer caps the headcount: the first N distinct collectors succeed, then the point is deactivated. Independent of the rarity tier.

activatePointRequest.description: Input for crownHunt.activatePoint (admin). Activation is a safety gate: the location must be explicitly confirmed safe and the approval note lands in the audit record.

crownHuntRarity.description: Auto-spawned crown rarity, ascending. Hand-placed points have no rarity.

crownHuntRarityCounts.description: Per-rarity histogram. Absent keys read as 0.

crownHuntLeaderboardEntry.description: One ranked leaderboard row. displayName is resolved from the public user profile at read time; seasonsWon is the member's lifetime championship count for 'N-time champion' display.

crownHuntLeaderboardEntryDoc.description: Firestore `crownHuntLeaderboardEntries/{scope}__{uid}` — the maintained per-scope counter (scope = 'alltime' | seasonId). Member-readable; ranks and names are composed by the reader.

crownHuntPersonalStats.description: A member's own Kronjakt statistics (readable by that member and admins). points/crowns/rank/streak derive from the Kronpoäng ledger (both crown kinds); byRarity/rarest cover auto-spawned crowns only.

seasonsWon.description: Lifetime first-place season finishes; grows every win.

crownHuntAdminStats.description: Admin dashboard totals for one scope ('alltime' | seasonId). Admin-only read.

crownHuntCellStat.description: Firestore `crownHuntCellStats/{cellKey}` — one 0.01° grid cell's spawn/collect counts for the admin heat/points map. cellKey is 'latIdx_lonIdx'; the cell centre is (latIdx*0.01, lonIdx*0.01). Admin-only read.

crownHuntSeasonWinner.description: A finalized podium finisher (top 3), with a displayName snapshot for the social screen.

crownHuntSeason.description: Firestore `crownHuntSeasons/{seasonId}` (seasonId = 'YYYY-MM', one Europe/Stockholm calendar month). Member-readable. winners/topStandings populate only once status is 'ended' (scheduled rollover), so the social screen can show 'last month's champions'.

crownSpawnRarity.description: Auto-spawn rarity. Rewards 10/25/100/500 KP; TTL 6/12/24/48 h.

crownCollectMode.description: How a spawned crown is collected. 'shared': many distinct members may each collect it once and it persists to its TTL. 'exclusive': the first taker removes it for everyone. Derived from rarity by the backend (common/uncommon/rare shared, legendary exclusive today). Clients may render exclusive crowns specially.

crownSpawnClaimResult.description: Result codes for crownHunt.claimSpawn. 'already_taken' = an EXCLUSIVE crown someone else already collected; 'already_collected' = a SHARED crown THIS member already collected (it stays on the map for others). Eligibility failures are codes with Swedish messages, not errors.

crownSpawnView.description: Member-facing view of a live auto-spawned crown (crownSpawns/{spawnId}). Backend-only fields (cellKey, areaId, approvedCellBy, safeLocationConfirmed, claim/risk metadata) are excluded — the client needs only where the crown is, what it is worth, how it is collected, and when it disappears. Members read live, unexpired crowns directly; all writes are backend-only.

crownSpawnAreaVertex.description: A WGS-84 vertex. 'lon' (not 'lng') to match the rest of these contracts.

crownSpawnAreaShape.description: The shape an admin drew for a marked spawn area — a discriminated union on 'type'. This schema enforces only the field-level constraints below (types, ranges, and the polygon vertex count 4..500). The following CROSS-FIELD rules are NOT expressible in JSON Schema and are enforced SERVER-SIDE by the crownHunt.createSpawnArea / updateSpawnArea callables, so a document that validates against this schema may still be rejected by the backend: the polygon ring must be CLOSED (first vertex equals last) with at least 3 DISTINCT vertices; a rectangle's bounds must satisfy north > south AND east > west (no antimeridian wrap); and any shape whose bounding box would span more than 20000 grid cells is rejected. Do not rely on this schema alone to accept a shape as spawnable.

crownSpawnArea.description: Admin view of a marked spawn area (crownSpawnAreas/{areaId}). NOT member-readable — an operational safety artefact, admin-read + client-write-denied in firestore.rules; all writes via the audited crownHunt.createSpawnArea/updateSpawnArea/deleteSpawnArea callables. The spawner places crowns at random points INSIDE the shape only while active AND safeAreaConfirmed are both true; ACTIVATING requires the safety confirmation in the same request. additionalProperties is TRUE here (unlike the strict create/update REQUEST schemas): the persisted Firestore document ALSO carries server-managed runtime fields not part of this client contract — the round-robin cursors lastSpawnPassAt and nextCellOffset, and the deactivation audit trio deactivatedByUserId / deactivatedAt / deactivationReason — so a consumer validating a directly-read area document is not tripped up by them. The crownHunt.listSpawnAreas response returns exactly the curated fields below.

poiCount.description: Count of cached OpenStreetMap safe-stop POIs (parking/fuel/charging) inside this area — the anchor points the spawner places crowns at instead of random in-shape points. 0 until the area's POI ingestion has run. Surfaced by crownHunt.listSpawnAreas so the admin UI can show 'N safe spots found in this area'; whenever it is shown the OSM attribution '© OpenStreetMap contributors' (ODbL) must appear alongside. Absent on documents created before this field; listSpawnAreas returns it as 0.

poisRefreshedAt.description: When the POI cache was last refreshed, or null if it never has been (a just-created area before ingestion, or after an Overpass failure that kept the previous cache).

createSpawnAreaRequest.description: Input for crownHunt.createSpawnArea (admin). Setting active:true REQUIRES safeAreaConfirmed:true in the same request.

updateSpawnAreaRequest.description: Input for crownHunt.updateSpawnArea (admin). At least one of shape/name/active/safeAreaConfirmed must be present; setting active:true REQUIRES safeAreaConfirmed:true in the same request. Re-drawing the shape or deactivating drains the area's live crowns.

deleteSpawnAreaRequest.description: Input for crownHunt.deleteSpawnArea (admin). Drains the area's live crowns, then removes the document.

listSpawnAreasRequest.description: Input for crownHunt.listSpawnAreas (admin). Both fields optional: activeOnly filters to currently-active areas; limit bounds the page (1..500, default 200).
